docs.title: nyx-usd
docs.text:
USD operations for Nyx graphs: open, create, inspect and edit USD stages with nodes, and save the result. There are nodes for stages, prims, attributes, metadata and time, composition (references, payloads, sublayers, variants), transforms, basic geometry and materials.

Nyx itself never imports pxr. The USD code runs in another interpreter that has USD (an OpenUSD build, usd-core, Maya, Houdini, Blender), which connects to Nyx through nyx-bridge. The nodes send it the work and bring the result back, so the same graph runs with any of those.

USD Client                                  <- starts the interpreter with USD
└── Remote Client
    └── Create Stage ─▶ Add Prim ─▶ Create Cube ─▶ Set Transform ─▶ Save Stage
If you want to... Read Install the plugin and the Python side, start a client User Guide Look up a node Nodes Add an operation or work on nyx-usd Developer Guide Look up a function of nyx_usd.ops API reference (see the navigation)

Requires Nyx, and an interpreter with USD (pxr) and Python 3.11 or newer. See also nyx-bridge-maya and nyx-bridge-blender for running the operations inside those applications.

docs.title: ops
docs.text:
USD operations run by Nyx nodes in an interpreter that has pxr.

Plain functions that take and return JSON data. Nothing here imports Nyx or the bridge, so the package works in any application shipping pxr (an OpenUSD build, Maya, Houdini, Blender).

A stage is identified by the identifier of its root layer, a string. The opened stages are kept in this package until they are closed, so one node can edit what the previous one opened. They stay open until close_stage or close_all, or the process ends.

The nodes call nyx_usd.ops.<name>, so every operation is imported here.

def add_inherit(stage: str, prim_path: str, class_path: str) -> str:
    """Make a prim inherit from a class prim.

    stage: str, prim_path: str, asset_path: str, target_prim: str = ""

    A payload is a reference that can be left unloaded.

        target_prim (str): prim of the file to load, its default prim if empty.

    else:

def bind_material(stage: str, prim_path: str, material_path: str) -> str:
    """Bind a material to a prim and what is below it.

    Args:
        stage (str): stage handle.

def copy_prim(stage: str, prim_path: str, new_path: str) -> str:
    """Copy a prim with everything below it, in the layer the stage edits.

    Args:
        stage (str): stage handle.
        prim_path (str): path of the prim.
        new_path (str): path of the copy. The prims above it are created if missing.

    Raises:
        ValueError: no prim at the path, or the layer has no spec to copy.

    Returns:
        str: handle of the stage.
    """
    get_prim(stage, prim_path)
    source, target = Sdf.Path(prim_path), Sdf.Path(new_path)
    layer = get_stage(stage).GetEditTarget().GetLayer()
    if not layer.GetPrimAtPath(source):
        raise ValueError(f"{prim_path} has no spec in {layer.identifier}")
    Sdf.CreatePrimInLayer(layer, target.GetParentPath())
    if not Sdf.CopySpec(layer, source, layer, target):
        raise ValueError(f"Can't copy {prim_path} to {new_path}")
    return stage

def create_material(
    stage: str, prim_path: str, diffuse_color: list[float] | None = None
) -> str:
    """Define a material with a UsdPreviewSurface shader.

    Args:
        stage (str): stage handle.
        prim_path (str): path of the material. The shader is `PreviewSurface` below it.
        diffuse_color (list[float] | None): red, green and blue, `[0.8, 0.8, 0.8]` if
            omitted.

    Raises:
        ValueError: the color doesn't have three numbers.

    Returns:
        str: handle of the stage.
    """
    color = _vector([0.8, 0.8, 0.8] if diffuse_color is None else diffuse_color, "color")
    usd_stage = get_stage(stage)
    material = UsdShade.Material.Define(usd_stage, prim_path)
    shader = UsdShade.Shader.Define(usd_stage, f"{prim_path}/PreviewSurface")
    shader.CreateIdAttr("UsdPreviewSurface")
    shader.CreateInput("diffuseColor", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Color3f).Set(Gf.Vec3f(*color))
    surface = shader.CreateOutput("surface", Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Token)
    material.CreateSurfaceOutput().ConnectToSource(surface)
    return stage

def create_mesh(
    stage: str,
    prim_path: str,
    points: list[list[float]],
    face_vertex_counts: list[int],
    face_vertex_indices: list[int],
) -> str:
    """Define a polygon mesh prim.

    Args:
        stage (str): stage handle.
        prim_path (str): path of the prim.
        points (list[list[float]]): position of every vertex, as x, y and z.
        face_vertex_counts (list[int]): number of vertices of every face.
        face_vertex_indices (list[int]): vertex of every corner of every face.

    Raises:
        ValueError: the counts and the indices don't fit, or an index is out of range.

    Returns:
        str: handle of the stage.
    """
    if sum(face_vertex_counts) != len(face_vertex_indices):
        raise ValueError(
            f"The faces have {sum(face_vertex_counts)} corners, "
            f"there are {len(face_vertex_indices)} indices"
        )
    if face_vertex_indices and not 0 <= min(face_vertex_indices) <= max(
        face_vertex_indices
    ) < len(points):
        raise ValueError(f"An index is outside of the {len(points)} points")
    mesh = UsdGeom.Mesh.Define(get_stage(stage), prim_path)
    mesh.GetPointsAttr().Set(
        Vt.Vec3fArray([Gf.Vec3f(*_vector(p, "point")) for p in points])
    )
    mesh.GetFaceVertexCountsAttr().Set(Vt.IntArray([int(c) for c in face_vertex_counts]))
    mesh.GetFaceVertexIndicesAttr().Set(
        Vt.IntArray([int(i) for i in face_vertex_indices])
    )
    return stage

def find_prims(stage: str, name_pattern: str, type_name: str = "") -> list[str]:
    """Find prims by name.

    Args:
        stage (str): stage handle.
        name_pattern (str): regular expression searched in the name of the prims, not
            their whole path.
        type_name (str): only the prims of this schema type, all if empty.

    Returns:
        list[str]: paths of the prims that match.
    """
    pattern = re.compile(name_pattern)
    return [
        str(prim.GetPath())
        for prim in get_stage(stage).Traverse()
        if pattern.search(prim.GetName())
        and (not type_name or prim.GetTypeName() == type_name)
    ]

def get_bounding_box(stage: str, prim_path: str) -> list[list[float]]:
    """Get the bounds of a prim and what is below it, in the world.

    Args:
        stage (str): stage handle.
        prim_path (str): path of the prim.

    Raises:
        ValueError: there is no prim at the path.

    Returns:
        list[list[float]]: the minimum and maximum corner. Empty bounds have a
            minimum larger than the maximum.
    """
    cache = UsdGeom.BBoxCache(Usd.TimeCode.Default(), [UsdGeom.Tokens.default_])
    box = cache.ComputeWorldBound(get_prim(stage, prim_path)).ComputeAlignedRange()
    return [list(box.GetMin()), list(box.GetMax())]

    stage: str,
    prim_path: str,
    translate: list[float] | None = None,
    rotate: list[float] | None = None,
    scale: list[float] | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Set the local transform of a prim, replacing the transform operations it has.

    Args:
        stage (str): stage handle.
        prim_path (str): path of the prim.
        translate (list[float] | None): x, y and z, `[0, 0, 0]` if omitted.
        rotate (list[float] | None): x, y and z rotation in degrees, `[0, 0, 0]` if
            omitted.

            have three numbers.

    translation = _vector([0, 0, 0] if translate is None else translate, "translate")
    rotation = _vector([0, 0, 0] if rotate is None else rotate, "rotate")
    scaling = _vector([1, 1, 1] if scale is None else scale, "scale")

    xformable.AddRotateXYZOp().Set(Gf.Vec3f(*rotation))
    xformable.AddScaleOp().Set(Gf.Vec3f(*scaling))

def get_attribute_of(
    prim: Usd.Prim, attr: str, type_name: str = "", create: bool = False
) -> Usd.Attribute:
    """Get an attribute of a prim, optionally creating it.

    Args:
        prim (Usd.Prim): prim holding the attribute.

        type_name (str): value type like `float` or `float3`, to create a missing
            attribute.
        create (bool): create the attribute if it is missing.

    Raises:
        ValueError: the attribute is missing and can't be created, because `create`
            is off or the type is unknown.

    Returns:
        Usd.Attribute: the attribute.

    attribute = prim.GetAttribute(attr)
    if attribute:
        return attribute
    if not create:
        raise ValueError(f"No attribute {attr!r} on {str(prim.GetPath())!r}")
    value_type = Sdf.ValueTypeNames.Find(type_name)
    if not value_type:
        raise ValueError(

            f"not {type_name!r}"

    return prim.CreateAttribute(attr, value_type)

def to_json(value: typing.Any) -> typing.Any:
    """Convert a USD value to JSON data.

    Args:
        value (Any): value of an attribute or of metadata.

    Returns:
        Any: JSON value. Vectors, matrices and arrays become lists, dictionaries
            stay dictionaries, what can't be converted its `str`.
    """
    if value is None or isinstance(value, (bool, int, float, str)):
        return value
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {str(key): to_json(each) for key, each in value.items()}
    if isinstance(value, (Gf.Matrix3d, Gf.Matrix4d, Gf.Matrix3f, Gf.Matrix4f)):
        return [list(row) for row in value]
    try:
        return [to_json(each) for each in value]
    except TypeError:
        return str(value)

def to_usd(value: typing.Any, type_name: Sdf.ValueTypeName) -> typing.Any:
    """Convert JSON data to what an attribute of a type takes.

    Args:
        value (Any): JSON value. Lists become vectors, matrices and arrays.
        type_name (Sdf.ValueTypeName): type of the attribute.

    Returns:
        Any: value for `Usd.Attribute.Set`.
    """
    if not isinstance(value, list):
        return value
    python_class = type_name.type.pythonClass
    if type_name.isArray:
        element = type_name.scalarType.type.pythonClass
        if element is not None and value and isinstance(value[0], list):
            value = [element(*each) for each in value]
        return python_class(value) if python_class is not None else value
    return python_class(*value) if python_class is not None else value

def create_mesh(
    stage: str,
    prim_path: str,
    points: list[list[float]],
    face_vertex_counts: list[int],
    face_vertex_indices: list[int],
) -> str:
    """Define a polygon mesh prim.

    Args:
        stage (str): stage handle.
        prim_path (str): path of the prim.
        points (list[list[float]]): position of every vertex, as x, y and z.
        face_vertex_counts (list[int]): number of vertices of every face.
        face_vertex_indices (list[int]): vertex of every corner of every face.

    Raises:
        ValueError: the counts and the indices don't fit, or an index is out of range.

    Returns:
        str: handle of the stage.
    """
    if sum(face_vertex_counts) != len(face_vertex_indices):
        raise ValueError(
            f"The faces have {sum(face_vertex_counts)} corners, "
            f"there are {len(face_vertex_indices)} indices"
        )
    if face_vertex_indices and not 0 <= min(face_vertex_indices) <= max(
        face_vertex_indices
    ) < len(points):
        raise ValueError(f"An index is outside of the {len(points)} points")
    mesh = UsdGeom.Mesh.Define(get_stage(stage), prim_path)
    mesh.GetPointsAttr().Set(
        Vt.Vec3fArray([Gf.Vec3f(*_vector(p, "point")) for p in points])
    )
    mesh.GetFaceVertexCountsAttr().Set(Vt.IntArray([int(c) for c in face_vertex_counts]))
    mesh.GetFaceVertexIndicesAttr().Set(
        Vt.IntArray([int(i) for i in face_vertex_indices])
    )
    return stage

def set_transform(
    stage: str,
    prim_path: str,
    translate: list[float] | None = None,
    rotate: list[float] | None = None,
    scale: list[float] | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Set the local transform of a prim, replacing the transform operations it has.

    Args:
        stage (str): stage handle.
        prim_path (str): path of the prim.
        translate (list[float] | None): x, y and z, `[0, 0, 0]` if omitted.
        rotate (list[float] | None): x, y and z rotation in degrees, `[0, 0, 0]` if
            omitted.
        scale (list[float] | None): x, y and z, `[1, 1, 1]` if omitted.

    Raises:
        ValueError: no prim at the path, it can't be transformed, or a list doesn't
            have three numbers.

    Returns:
        str: handle of the stage.
    """
    translation = _vector([0, 0, 0] if translate is None else translate, "translate")
    rotation = _vector([0, 0, 0] if rotate is None else rotate, "rotate")
    scaling = _vector([1, 1, 1] if scale is None else scale, "scale")
    xformable = _xformable(stage, prim_path)
    xformable.ClearXformOpOrder()
    xformable.AddTranslateOp().Set(Gf.Vec3d(*translation))
    xformable.AddRotateXYZOp().Set(Gf.Vec3f(*rotation))
    xformable.AddScaleOp().Set(Gf.Vec3f(*scaling))
    return stage

def copy_prim(stage: str, prim_path: str, new_path: str) -> str:

    Args:
        stage (str): stage handle.
        prim_path (str): path of the prim.

    Raises:
        ValueError: no prim at the path, or the layer has no spec to copy.

    Returns:

    get_prim(stage, prim_path)
    source, target = Sdf.Path(prim_path), Sdf.Path(new_path)

    if not layer.GetPrimAtPath(source):

    Sdf.CreatePrimInLayer(layer, target.GetParentPath())
    if not Sdf.CopySpec(layer, source, layer, target):
        raise ValueError(f"Can't copy {prim_path} to {new_path}")
    return stage

            their whole path.
        type_name (str): only the prims of this schema type, all if empty.

    """
    pattern = re.compile(name_pattern)
    return [

        for prim in get_stage(stage).Traverse()
        if pattern.search(prim.GetName())
        and (not type_name or prim.GetTypeName() == type_name)
    ]

docs.title: Developer Guide
docs.text: This guide is for people who work on nyx-usd itself.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
uv sync
make check        # ruff + pytest
make qrc          # compile the Qt resources of the plugin (icons)
make mkdocs       # serve these docs

make help lists every target. Ruff uses a line length of 89 and the E, F and UP rules. Docstrings are Google style: the API reference is generated from them.

The tests of the operations need pxr, which usd-core (a dev dependency) provides, see Testing.

Important

The two halves of the project must stay apart:

  • nyx_usd (the operations) imports only pxr and the standard library. Never nyx, nyx_bridge or Qt: it has to run in Maya, Blender and a bare USD build.
  • plugins/usd_plugin (the nodes) imports only nyx.api.v1 and the standard library. Never pxr: Nyx runs a Python USD is not built for, and importing it there can crash the process.

docs.title: Pages

docs.title: Adding an operation
docs.text: A new operation is a function, a node spec and tests. Say it is set_foo in the area prims.

docs.title: 1. The function
docs.text:
In the module of its area (src/nyx_usd/ops/prims.py):

def set_foo(stage: str, prim_path: str, foo: float = 1.0) -> str:
    """Set the foo of a prim.

    Args:
        stage (str): stage handle.
        prim_path (str): path of the prim.
        foo (float): the foo.

    Raises:
        ValueError: there is no prim at the path.

    Returns:
        str: handle of the stage.
    """
    prim = get_prim(stage, prim_path)
    ...
    return stage

Rules:

  • stage comes first, a handle. Use get_stage and get_prim from _common, they raise a clear ValueError.
  • JSON in, JSON out. Arguments are numbers, strings, booleans, lists and dictionaries. Return the same, with to_json for USD values. Convert lists with to_usd when an attribute needs a vector or an array.
  • A function that edits returns the handle (Returns: str: handle of the stage.), so nodes chain. A function that reads returns the value.
  • Fail with ValueError and a message that names the path or value. Catch the exceptions of pxr that you can explain, a Tf error says little. Check a result False from Set... and Apply: USD often reports failure that way.
  • Only pxr and the standard library, and only long-lived USD APIs (Usd, Sdf, UsdGeom, UsdShade): the same function has to work with the older USD of Maya and Houdini.
  • No newer syntax than Python 3.11. Use from __future__ import annotations.
  • Docstrings in Google style. They are the API reference.

Then import it in src/nyx_usd/ops/__init__.py, in the group of its module and in __all__. The nodes call nyx_usd.ops.set_foo, so a function that is not there is not found.

docs.title: 2. The node
docs.text:
In the module of the area in plugins/usd_plugin/nodes/specs/, add an OperationSpec to SPECS:

OperationSpec(
    "set_foo",                  # the function name, also the node type id usd:set_foo
    "Set Foo",                  # shown in the palette
    "Sets the foo of a prim.",  # the description
    (
        STAGE_PARAM,
        PRIM_PARAM,
        Param("foo", FLOAT, 1.0, "The foo."),
    ),
    STRING,                     # datatype of the response
    ("prim",),                  # tags
),
  • The params match the function: the same names, in the same order. A node passes them as keyword arguments, a mismatch fails at run time.
  • Use STAGE_PARAM, PRIM_PARAM, ATTR_PARAM and the datatypes of specs/common.py where they fit. The datatype of a stage handle is STRING.
  • Give a default for every input the user would not want to be empty. Lists as defaults are copied for each node.
  • Tags are what the operation is about (prim, attribute, composition, transform, geometry, shading, ...). Reuse the existing ones, they are searchable as tags:prim.
  • A new area is a new module in specs/ that defines SPECS, and a line in nodes/operations.py.

docs.title: 3. Tests
docs.text: In tests/test_ops/test_<area>.py, against real USD. Cover the normal result and each ValueError. The stage fixture is an empty stage in memory and stages are closed after each test. See Testing.

docs.title: 4. Check it
docs.text:
make check

Then check the node side with Nyx, see Testing: the spec matches the signature, the node can be created, and a graph runs it.

docs.title: 5. Document it
docs.text:
• Add a row for the node to the table in docs/user/nodes/<area>.md, with the inputs, output and description of the spec. The tables are written by hand: keep them in step with the specs.
  • If the node has a behaviour users trip over, add a line to the notes of that page.
  • A user-visible addition goes in CHANGELOG.rst when releasing, see Releasing.

docs.title: Two halves in two interpreters
docs.text:
nyx_usd plugins/usd_plugin Runs in The client: an interpreter with pxr Nyx (Python 3.14) Imports pxr, the standard library nyx.api.v1, the standard library Is Plain functions, JSON in and out One node class per function Packaged In the wheel (sowwic-nyx-usd) No: the plugins folder is put on NYX_PLUGIN_PATH

They meet at one place: the name and arguments of a function of nyx_usd.ops.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
Every function in ops takes a stage handle first, and gets JSON values only (numbers, strings, booleans, lists, dictionaries). A function that edits a stage returns its handle, so nodes chain; a function that reads returns the value.

_common.STAGES maps handles to opened Usd.Stage objects. A handle is the identifier of the root layer. The opened stages live as long as the process, until close_stage or close_all. get_stage and get_prim raise a ValueError with the handle or path in the message, which Nyx shows on the node.

_common.to_usd turns a JSON list into the vector, matrix or array an attribute type calls for, and to_json does the opposite for what is read, so a Vec3f is [x, y, z] and a Matrix4d a list of rows.

The functions are imported in ops/__init__.py, because that is what the nodes call.

docs.title: Nodes
docs.text:
create_node_class makes one UsdNode subclass from an OperationSpec. UsdNode extends Nyx's RemoteActionNode, which already knows how to send code to the client of the enclosing Remote Client node, and overrides its hooks:

  1. setup adds flow, one input per Param, timeout and response. List defaults are copied for every node, so nodes don't share one list.
  2. build_args reads the inputs into a dictionary.

  3. build_script returns the code the client runs:

    import nyx_usd.ops
result = nyx_usd.ops.<name>(**{name: globals()[name] for name in [...]})

  4. The inherited execute sends it with the arguments as variables, waits (with the timeout) and passes the value assigned to result to handle_response, which puts it in response.

execute is not overridden, so the error handling is the one of RemoteActionNode: a function that raises comes back as a RemoteExecutionError with its message.

OperationSpec.tags become the tags of the node ({"usd", "bridge", *tags}), which the palette search understands as tags:<tag>. The Param datatypes come from CoreDatatypes. A stage handle is a plain core:string, there is no datatype of its own.

docs.title: The USD Client node
docs.text:
UsdClientNode (usd_client.py) extends Nyx's LaunchProcessNode. It reuses all of it, and changes two things:

  • The command input is turned into python (renamed in setup), keeping its place in the node.
  • _build_arguments returns [python, "-c", CLIENT_SOURCE] instead of splitting a command line. The interpreter is the input, or NYX_USD_PYTHON of the environment of the process, and it fails with a clear message if there is neither.

CLIENT_SOURCE is a small nyx_bridge client with the kind usd, connecting under the name Launch Process put in NYX_BRIDGE_CLIENT_NAME (the node waits for exactly that name). The address and token come from the environment Launch Process sets.

docs.title: How Nyx loads the plugin
docs.text:
Nyx finds nyx_plugin.py files under the folders of NYX_PLUGIN_PATH. It imports the file with the name of its folder as the package, so the relative imports (from .nodes.operations import OPERATIONS) work with no __init__.py files, as in the Nyx stdlib. The modules are named usd_plugin.nyx_plugin.*. Folders like nodes/ and specs/ are namespace packages.

nyx_plugin.py imports resources_rc for its side effect: it registers the icons under :/usd/, which the node classes use as get_type_icon.

docs.title: Python versions
docs.text: nyx_usd supports Python 3.11 and newer, the oldest Python of the applications it runs in (Maya 2026 is 3.11). Keep newer syntax out of ops. The plugin runs in Nyx's Python.

docs.title: Branches and versions
docs.text:
develop is the default and PR branch; main is the release branch. Work on a feature branch named after the GitHub issue.

The version lives in VERSION. make update-version copies it into pyproject.toml (and make build does that first). Add a section for it at the top of CHANGELOG.rst, one bullet per user-visible change with the issue number where there is one: new nodes, new inputs, changed behaviour of an operation.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
make release VERSION=1.2.3 [RELEASE_TITLE="..."]

Runs the release script of sowwic/gh-workflows: it tags main, pushes, and merges back into develop. The tag triggers .github/workflows/release.yml, which creates the GitHub release from the changelog section.

docs.title: What gets released
docs.text:
Part Where users get it nyx_usd, the operations The package sowwic-nyx-usd (PyPI), which they install in the interpreter with USD. plugins/usd_plugin, the nodes Not in the package. Users put the plugins folder of a checkout or of the release's source archive on NYX_PLUGIN_PATH.

The plugin and the package have to be of the same version: a node calls the function of that name with those arguments. Say so in the changelog when an operation changes.

docs.title: Publishing to PyPI
docs.text:
The distribution is called sowwic-nyx-usd and imports as nyx_usd. The targets come from the general/pypi module of sowwic/makefiles:

make pypi-publish-dev     # build and upload to TestPyPI
make pypi-publish         # build and upload to PyPI

Both run clean and build first, so only a fresh build is uploaded. uv publish reads the token from UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN, so put it in the environment for the run, not in a file:

UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN=pypi-... make pypi-publish

The first upload needs an account-wide token, a token for one project can only be made once it exists. A published version can't be replaced: to fix a bad release, bump VERSION and publish again, to hide one, yank it on pypi.org.

docs.title: CI
docs.text: Workflows in .github/workflows/ are thin callers of the shared ones in sowwic/gh-workflows: tests, lint, docs deployment to GitHub Pages (on main) and the release.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
make pytest                                              # everything, with coverage
uv run pytest tests/test_ops/test_prims.py::test_rename_prim   # one test
make pytest-pdb                                          # verbose, pdb on failure
make check                                               # lint and tests

Coverage (--cov=nyx_usd) is on by default. The tests of the operations run against real USD: usd-core is in the dev dependency group. Without pxr installed, tests/conftest.py leaves tests/test_ops/ out instead of failing.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text: File Covers tests/test_package.py The package imports. tests/test_ops/test_stages.py Open, create, save, export and close. tests/test_ops/test_prims.py Add, remove, query, find, rename, move, copy, active, kind, prim metadata. tests/test_ops/test_attributes.py Set and get, creating with a type, vectors and arrays, time samples, list, remove. tests/test_ops/test_stage_settings.py Stage metadata, time range, fps, axis, units, default prim, stage info. tests/test_ops/test_composition.py References, payloads, inherits, sublayers, variants, export and flatten. tests/test_ops/test_geometry.py Transforms, bounds, visibility, purpose, shapes, meshes, materials.

docs.title: Fixtures
docs.text:
• output_dir (tests/conftest.py): .test_output/ in the working directory, for files the tests write.
  • stage (tests/test_ops/conftest.py): the handle of an empty stage in memory.
  • close_stages (autouse, same file): closes every stage after each test, so tests don't see each other's stages.

docs.title: What to cover
docs.text:
• Every operation: the normal result, and each ValueError it can raise, with pytest.raises(..., match=...) on a part of the message.
  • A write goes through USD again: read it back with another operation, or reopen the saved file. Don't only check that nothing failed.
  • Values that cross the JSON boundary: vectors, matrices and arrays in both directions.
  • Composition tests check the effect: that a reference, payload, inherit or variant changes what get_attribute gives.
  • Remember that a value set on a prim directly is stronger than a variant's, so a variant test starts from a prim without that value.
  • Anything that needs the Python API of USD directly (for example to author inside a variant) can use nyx_usd.ops._common.get_stage(handle) and get_prim.

docs.title: Checking the plugin with Nyx
docs.text:
The nodes import Nyx, which is not a dependency of this project, so pytest does not cover them. Check them with the environment of the Nyx repository, with Nyx started offscreen and the plugin on its path.

# From the Nyx repository: NYX_PLUGIN_PATH=/path/to/nyx-usd/plugins uv run python check.py
import ast, os, pathlib, sys

os.environ["QT_QPA_PLATFORM"] = "offscreen"
from nyx.application import NyxApplication

app = NyxApplication()                      # loads the plugins of NYX_PLUGIN_PATH

signatures = {}
for module in pathlib.Path("/path/to/nyx-usd/src/nyx_usd/ops").glob("*.py"):
    if module.name.startswith("_"):
        continue
    for node in ast.parse(module.read_text()).body:
        if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef) and not node.name.startswith("_"):
            signatures[node.name] = [arg.arg for arg in node.args.args]

specs = sys.modules["usd_plugin.nyx_plugin.nodes.operations"].OPERATIONS
print([s.name for s in specs if signatures.get(s.name) != [p.name for p in s.params]])
print(set(signatures) - {s.name for s in specs})   # only close_all has no node

The first line should print [] (no mismatch) and the second {'close_all'}. After that:

  1. Create every node with create_node(stage, f"usd:{spec.name}") from stage_helpers of the Nyx tests. It fails if a spec is invalid.
  2. Run a graph. Start the bridge server of the app session (app.session.start_bridge_server()), build USD Client (with python and env set to an interpreter with USD and PYTHONPATH for nyx_usd and nyx_bridge) with a Remote Client inside, chain a few nodes, and run the stage with stage.crawler.start(). Read the response of the nodes you want to check.

Do it for a change to the plugin side, or to the arguments of a function. A change inside a function only needs make check.

docs.title: CI
docs.text: .github/workflows/unit_tests.yml calls the shared Python test workflow (sowwic/gh-workflows) on Python 3.12, and code_quality.yml the lint one. Local development uses 3.12 too (.python-version), but the project supports Python 3.11, the Python of Maya 2026: keep newer syntax out of nyx_usd.

docs.title: User Guide
docs.text: This guide is for people who use the USD nodes in Nyx.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text: Page What you learn Installation The plugin for Nyx, nyx_usd for the interpreter with USD, and checking both. Starting a client The USD Client node, Launch Process, starting one by hand, Maya and Blender. Using the nodes Stage handles, wiring, errors, and two worked examples. Nodes Every node: inputs, output and what it does, by area.

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
Nyx (Python 3.14)                        Interpreter with USD
┌──────────────────────┐   it connects out   ┌──────────────────────┐
│ Bridge server        │ ◀────────────────── │ nyx_bridge client    │
│ USD nodes            │ ── operation ─────▶ │ imports nyx_usd.ops  │
│                      │ ◀── result ──────── │ and runs it on pxr   │
└──────────────────────┘                     └──────────────────────┘
  1. Nyx listens on a local port and holds a secret token.
  2. An interpreter that has USD starts a client, which connects to Nyx. The USD Client node can start it for you.
  3. A USD node inside a Remote Client node sends the name of an operation and its inputs. The client calls nyx_usd.ops.<operation>, which uses pxr, and answers with the result.

The stages live in the client, not in Nyx. What travels between nodes is a stage handle, a string naming an opened stage, see Using the nodes.

Protocol and server details are in the nyx-bridge documentation.

docs.title: Stage handles
docs.text:
Opening or creating a stage happens in the client. What the node gives you back is a stage handle: a string that names the opened stage (it is the identifier of its root layer). Pass it to the stage input of every other node that works on that stage.

  • Open Stage and Create Stage output a handle.
  • Nodes that change a stage (Add Prim, Set Attribute, ...) take a handle and output the same handle, so you can chain them: wire the response of one to the stage of the next.
  • Nodes that read (List Prims, Get Attribute, ...) take a handle and output the value. They don't give the handle back, so keep the wire from the node before.
  • Save Stage writes the stage to its file, or exports it to another file.
  • Close Stage closes the stage in the client without saving it.

Changes only exist in the client until you save. Closing a stage without saving drops them.

docs.title: Wiring a graph
docs.text:
Every node has a flow input and output like other Nyx nodes, a timeout (seconds to wait for the answer, 30 by default, 0 or less waits forever) and a response output.

  1. Put a USD Client node, or a Launch Process node, or nothing if you start the client yourself, see Starting a client.
  2. Put a Remote Client node inside it.
  3. Put the USD nodes inside the Remote Client, chain their flow, and wire the response of the node that gives the stage to the stage input of the next ones.

Text inputs are taken as typed: /World/cube is the path, no quotes needed. List inputs take a list, like [1, 2, 3].

If an operation fails, the node fails with the message of the error from the client, for example No prim at '/World/cube' in '...', Stage is not open: ..., or the message of USD itself.

docs.title: Example: build a scene
docs.text:
USD Client
└── Remote Client
    ├── Create Stage       path = /tmp/scene.usda
    ├── Add Prim           prim_path = /World             type_name = Xform
    ├── Create Cube        prim_path = /World/cube        size = 2
    ├── Set Transform      prim_path = /World/cube        translate = [10, 0, 0]
    ├── Set Default Prim   prim_path = /World
    └── Save Stage

Wire the response of each node into the stage of the next one. The file written is:

#usda 1.0
(
    defaultPrim = "World"
    upAxis = "Y"
)

def Xform "World"
{
    def Cube "cube"
    {
        double size = 2
        float3 xformOp:rotateXYZ = (0, 0, 0)
        float3 xformOp:scale = (1, 1, 1)
        double3 xformOp:translate = (10, 0, 0)
        uniform token[] xformOpOrder = ["xformOp:translate", "xformOp:rotateXYZ", "xformOp:scale"]
    }
}

Add a Get Bounding Box node on /World/cube and its response is [[9, -1, -1], [11, 1, 1]].

docs.title: Example: look into a file
docs.text:
USD Client
└── Remote Client
    ├── Open Stage         path = /path/to/file.usd
    ├── Get Stage Info                      -> response: a dictionary
    ├── List Prims         type_name = Mesh -> response: a list of paths
    └── Get Attribute      prim_path = /World/mesh   attr = points

Get Stage Info gives root_layer, default_prim, up_axis, meters_per_unit, fps, start, end and prim_count. Wire the response of Open Stage to the stage of each of the nodes that read.

docs.title: Things to know
docs.text:
• Parents have no type. Add Prim with /World/cube creates /World without a type if it is missing, and a prim without a type can't be transformed. Add /World first, as an Xform, then the prims below it.
  • Local values win over variants. A value set directly on a prim is stronger than the value a variant gives, so an attribute you want a variant to control must not be set on the prim itself.
  • Rename, Move and Copy Prim work on the layer the stage edits, the root layer of a stage you opened. A prim that only exists through a reference or payload has nothing to rename or move there.
  • Values are JSON. Inputs and outputs are numbers, text, booleans, lists and dictionaries. Vectors, matrices and arrays come out as lists, and lists are accepted where an attribute needs a vector or an array, for example [1, 0.5, 0] for a color3f.
  • Attributes made on the fly. Set Attribute creates an attribute that is missing when you give its type_name, such as float, float3, color3f, token or string[].
  • Find the nodes by tag. Search the palette for tags:prim, tags:composition and so on, see Nodes.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
There are two halves to set up, in two different Pythons:

Half Where it runs What it needs The plugin: the nodes Nyx Nothing to install. Nyx finds it through NYX_PLUGIN_PATH. The operations: nyx_usd An interpreter with USD pxr, nyx-bridge and nyx_usd.

Important

Do not try to import pxr in Nyx's own Python. USD is compiled for one Python and loading it into another one can crash the process (a segmentation fault). That is why the operations run in a separate interpreter.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Nyx.
  • An interpreter with USD: an OpenUSD build, the usd-core package, or the Python of Maya, Houdini or Blender. Python 3.11 or newer.
  • uv (or pip) to install the Python packages.

docs.title: 1. The plugin for Nyx
docs.text:
The plugin is the plugins folder of this repository. Tell Nyx where it is, then start Nyx:

NYX_PLUGIN_PATH=/path/to/nyx-usd/plugins nyx

NYX_PLUGIN_PATH takes several folders, separated by : (; on Windows). To avoid the variable, add the folder to the plugin_paths value of the Nyx configuration instead.

The nodes are in the USD section of the palette. Their icon is the USD logo.

docs.title: 2. The operations for the interpreter with USD
docs.text:
In the interpreter that has pxr, install nyx_usd and nyx-bridge:

uv pip install sowwic-nyx-bridge
uv pip install -e /path/to/nyx-usd      # or: pip install /path/to/nyx-usd

nyx_usd has no dependencies of its own, it uses the pxr the interpreter provides. Without installing it you can put /path/to/nyx-usd/src on that interpreter's PYTHONPATH.

Check it from a shell, using the interpreter you will give to Nyx:

/path/to/usd/python -c "import pxr, nyx_bridge, nyx_usd; print('ok')"

If your USD build needs paths in the environment (PYTHONPATH, PATH), set them in the shell Nyx starts from, or in the env input of the node that starts the client, see Starting a client.

docs.title: Maya, Blender and Houdini
docs.text:
These applications ship pxr, so their interpreter only needs nyx_usd importable (and the client of that application, see Starting a client).

Note

In Maya, pxr can be imported once the mayaUsdPlugin is loaded: cmds.loadPlugin("mayaUsdPlugin"). Do this before running the nodes.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Check The nodes are not in the palette Nyx was started without NYX_PLUGIN_PATH, or it points at the repository root instead of plugins. The log lists the plugins it loads. No module named 'nyx_usd' on a USD node nyx_usd is not importable in the client's interpreter, see step 2. No module named 'pxr' on a USD node That interpreter has no USD, or its PYTHONPATH / PATH for the USD build is missing. No module named 'nyx_bridge' when the client starts Install sowwic-nyx-bridge in that interpreter. The Nyx process crashes on import pxr pxr was imported into Nyx's Python. Only the client's interpreter should have it. no interpreter, set python or $NYX_USD_PYTHON The USD Client node has no interpreter, see Starting a client. A USD node fails right away, saying it is not inside a Remote Client Put the node inside a Remote Client node. A Remote Client waits and times out No client connected. Is the bridge server running in Nyx, and the client started?

docs.title: Starting a client
docs.text: The USD nodes need a client: a running interpreter with USD that is connected to Nyx. Pick one of the ways below. In every case the nodes go inside a Remote Client node, which waits for the client and hands it to the nodes inside of it.

docs.title: The USD Client node
docs.text:
The simplest way. USD Client (usd:client) starts the interpreter for you, waits until it has connected, runs the nodes inside of it, and stops the process when they are done. It is a Launch Process node that builds the command itself.

USD Client      python = /path/to/usd/python
└── Remote Client
    └── Create Stage ─▶ ... ─▶ Save Stage
Input Meaning python The interpreter that has USD. If empty, the NYX_USD_PYTHON environment variable is used. env A dictionary of environment variables added to the ones of Nyx. Use it for PYTHONPATH and the like. working_directory Folder to run in. Empty uses the current one. client_name Name the client connects as. Empty makes one up. wait_for_client Wait until the client has connected before the nodes inside run. On by default. timeout Seconds to wait for it to connect. 0 or less waits forever. Output Meaning client The name the client connected as. process_id The id of the process.

The interpreter needs pxr, nyx-bridge and nyx_usd, see Installation. If they are found through environment variables, add them to env, for example:

{
  "PYTHONPATH": "/path/to/nyx-usd/src:/path/to/openusd/lib/python"
}

Note

env is added to the environment of Nyx, and a variable of the same name is replaced, not extended. Write the whole PYTHONPATH you need.

Set NYX_USD_PYTHON in the shell you start Nyx from to leave python empty in every graph:

export NYX_USD_PYTHON=/path/to/usd/python

Leave client_name and client_kind empty on the Remote Client inside of it: inside a USD Client node it uses the process that node started.

docs.title: A Launch Process node
docs.text:
The same thing with the generic node, when you want to control the command. Put this in its command input, with USD_PYTHON set in the environment or in env:

$USD_PYTHON -c "from nyx_bridge.client import NyxClient; NyxClient(name='$NYX_BRIDGE_CLIENT_NAME', reconnect=False).serve_forever()"

Launch Process gives the process the address and token of Nyx and the name it has to connect as (NYX_BRIDGE_ADDRESS, NYX_BRIDGE_TOKEN, NYX_BRIDGE_CLIENT_NAME). The client has to use that name, or Nyx keeps waiting for it. $NAME in the command is replaced with the variable of that name.

docs.title: By hand
docs.text:
Start a client yourself when the interpreter is already running, or lives on another machine. In that interpreter:

from nyx_bridge.client import NyxClient

NyxClient(name="usd").serve_forever()

It keeps trying to reach Nyx and connects again if the connection drops. It finds Nyx through the environment or the address file Nyx writes, see Finding the server. In Nyx, give the Remote Client the name: client_name = usd.

docs.title: Maya and Blender
docs.text:
The applications have their own clients, nyx-bridge-maya and nyx-bridge-blender. Connect the application, make nyx_usd importable in its Python (see Installation), and select it with client_kind on the Remote Client:

Application client_kind Maya maya Blender blender

The graph does not change: only the Remote Client node does. Inside the application the operations run on its main thread, like the other code Nyx sends.

docs.title: Which client does a Remote Client use?
docs.text: Remote Client is... It uses Inside a USD Client or Launch Process node, client_name and client_kind empty The process that node started. Anywhere, with client_name set The client of that name. Anywhere, with client_kind set The one connected client of that kind. If several match it fails instead of choosing, so code never goes to the wrong application: give a name.

docs.title: How long things live
docs.text: The stages a client has opened stay open until a Close Stage node closes them, or until the client ends. A client started by a USD Client or Launch Process node ends when the nodes inside of it are done. A client you started by hand keeps its stages while it runs, so close what you no longer need.

docs.title: Nodes
docs.text:
All the nodes are in the USD section of the palette. They go inside a Remote Client node, see Using the nodes.

Page Nodes Tags Stages Open, create, save and close a stage. stage Prims Add, remove, rename, move, copy, find and query prims, kind, active, metadata. prim, metadata Attributes Set and get attributes, over time, list, remove. attribute, time Stage settings Metadata, time range, fps, up axis, units, default prim, stage info. stage, settings, time, metadata Composition References, payloads, inherits, sublayers, variants, export and flatten. composition, layers, variants, export Transforms, geometry, shading Transforms, bounds, visibility, shapes, meshes, materials. transform, geometry, shading

The USD Client node is described in Starting a client.

docs.title: Finding nodes
docs.text: Every node has tags, shown on its palette item. Type a tag in the search field of the palette as tags:prim and only the nodes with that tag are listed. tags:usd lists them all.

docs.title: What every node has
docs.text:
Part Meaning flow Execution order, like other nodes. The inputs of the table The arguments of the operation. The stage input takes a stage handle. timeout Seconds to wait for the client's answer before failing. 30 by default, 0 or less waits forever. response What the operation gives back.

In the tables, the Output is stage when the node gives the handle of the stage it changed (chain it into the next node), none when there is nothing to give, and otherwise the kind of value: string, bool, list, dict or any. A value after = is the default of an input; inputs without one start empty.

docs.title: Attribute nodes
docs.text:
Tags: attribute, time

Read and write the attributes of a prim, with or without a time.

Node Inputs Output What it does Set Attributeusd:set_attribute stageprim_path = "/"attrvaluetype_name stage Sets the value of an attribute, creating it when a type is given. Get Attributeusd:get_attribute stageprim_path = "/"attr any Reads the value of an attribute. Set Attribute At Timeusd:set_attribute_at_time stageprim_path = "/"attrvaluetime = 0.0type_name stage Sets the value of an attribute at a time, creating it when a type is given. Get Attribute At Timeusd:get_attribute_at_time stageprim_path = "/"attrtime = 0.0 any Reads the value of an attribute at a time, interpolated between samples. Get Time Samplesusd:get_time_samples stageprim_path = "/"attr list Lists the times an attribute has a value at. List Attributesusd:list_attributes stageprim_path = "/" list Lists the names of the attributes of a prim. Remove Attributeusd:remove_attribute stageprim_path = "/"attr stage Removes an attribute from the layer the stage edits.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Set Attribute sets an existing attribute. To make one, give its type_name, the USD value type: float, int, bool, string, token, float3, color3f, point3f[], int[] and so on. Without it, a missing attribute is an error.
  • A list value becomes what the attribute needs: a vector ([1, 0.5, 0] for a color3f), a matrix or an array. Lists of lists make arrays of vectors, like the points of a mesh.
  • Get Attribute gives numbers and text as they are, and vectors, matrices and arrays as lists. An attribute without a value gives nothing.
  • The time nodes use time codes, the unit of the stage (frames at the fps of the stage). Get Attribute At Time interpolates between samples. Get Time Samples gives an empty list for an attribute that is not animated.
  • List Attributes includes the attributes the schema of the prim defines, not only the ones that have a value.
  • Remove Attribute removes the attribute from the layer the stage edits.

docs.title: Composition nodes
docs.text:
Tags: composition, layers, variants, export

Build a scene out of other files and layers, choose between variants, and get the result as text or a file.

Node Inputs Output What it does Add Referenceusd:add_reference stageprim_path = "/"asset_pathtarget_prim stage References a USD file on a prim. Add Payloadusd:add_payload stageprim_path = "/"asset_pathtarget_prim stage Adds a payload of a USD file to a prim, a reference that can stay unloaded. Add Inheritusd:add_inherit stageprim_path = "/"class_path stage Makes a prim inherit from a class prim. Add Sublayerusd:add_sublayer stagelayer_path stage Adds a layer file to the sublayers of the root layer. Remove Sublayerusd:remove_sublayer stagelayer_path stage Removes a layer from the sublayers of the root layer. List Sublayersusd:list_sublayers stage list Lists the sublayers of the root layer. Add Variant Setusd:add_variant_set stageprim_path = "/"set_namevariants = [] stage Adds a variant set with variants to a prim. Set Variant Selectionusd:set_variant_selection stageprim_path = "/"set_namevariant stage Selects a variant of a variant set. Get Variantsusd:get_variants stageprim_path = "/" dict Describes the variant sets of a prim: their variants and selection. Export To Stringusd:export_to_string stageflatten = False string Gets the USD text of a stage, optionally flattened into one layer. Flatten Stageusd:flatten_stage stagepath string Composes a stage into one layer and writes it to a file.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Add Reference and Add Payload take a file and, optionally, a target_prim in it. Without a target, the default prim of that file is used, so a file without one gives nothing: set its default prim, or give the target. A payload is a reference that can be left unloaded; here it is loaded.
  • Add Inherit points the prim at a class prim, usually named with a leading underscore like /_class_asset. It has no effect until that prim exists.
  • Add Sublayer adds the layer as the weakest of the root layer. Remove Sublayer takes the path as it was added.
  • Add Variant Set adds the set and its variants, and keeps variants it already has. Set Variant Selection with an empty variant clears the selection. Get Variants gives, for every set, its variants and its selection.
  • Export To String gives the USDA text of the root layer. With flatten the whole stage is composed into one layer first, with references, payloads and variants resolved. Flatten Stage writes that to a file.

docs.title: Transform, geometry and shading nodes
docs.text:
Tags: transform, geometry, shading

Move prims, make basic shapes and meshes, and give them materials.

Node Inputs Output What it does Set Transformusd:set_transform stageprim_path = "/"translate = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]rotate = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]scale = [1.0, 1.0, 1.0] stage Sets the local transform of a prim, replacing its transform operations. Get Transformusd:get_transform stageprim_path = "/" list Gets the local transform of a prim as a 4x4 matrix. Get World Transformusd:get_world_transform stageprim_path = "/" list Gets the transform of a prim in the world as a 4x4 matrix. Get Bounding Boxusd:get_bounding_box stageprim_path = "/" list Gets the bounds of a prim and what is below it, in the world. Set Visibilityusd:set_visibility stageprim_path = "/"visible = True stage Shows or hides a prim and what is below it. Set Purposeusd:set_purpose stageprim_path = "/"purpose = "default" stage Sets what a prim is drawn for: default, render, proxy or guide. Create Cubeusd:create_cube stageprim_path = "/"size = 1.0 stage Defines a cube prim. Create Sphereusd:create_sphere stageprim_path = "/"radius = 1.0 stage Defines a sphere prim. Create Meshusd:create_mesh stageprim_path = "/"points = []face_vertex_counts = []face_vertex_indices = [] stage Defines a polygon mesh prim. Create Materialusd:create_material stageprim_path = "/"diffuse_color = [0.8, 0.8, 0.8] stage Defines a material with a UsdPreviewSurface shader. Bind Materialusd:bind_material stageprim_path = "/"material_path stage Binds a material to a prim and what is below it.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Set Transform replaces the transform operations of the prim with a translate, a rotate (X, Y, Z in degrees) and a scale, applied in that order. Only the prims of types that can be transformed, like Xform, Cube and Mesh, work.
  • Get Transform and Get World Transform give a 4x4 matrix as a list of rows. The translation is the last row: [10, 0, 0, 1]. The world transform includes the parents.
  • Get Bounding Box gives [[min x, y, z], [max x, y, z]] of the prim and what is below it, in the world. A prim with nothing to measure has a minimum larger than its maximum.
  • Set Visibility needs a prim that is drawable (Imageable), Set Purpose takes default, render, proxy or guide.
  • Create Mesh checks that the counts add up to the indices and that every index is one of the points.
  • Create Material makes a material with a UsdPreviewSurface shader named PreviewSurface below it, with the diffuse_color given. Bind Material binds a material to a prim and what is below it, and fails if the path is not a material.

docs.title: Prim nodes
docs.text:
Tags: prim, metadata

Create, query and edit prims: the objects of a stage, found by their path like /World/cube.

Node Inputs Output What it does Add Primusd:add_prim stageprim_path = "/"type_name = "Xform" stage Defines a prim, and the prims above it without a type if they are missing. Remove Primusd:remove_prim stageprim_path = "/" stage Removes a prim from the stage. List Primsusd:list_prims stagetype_name list Lists the prim paths of a stage. Has Primusd:has_prim stageprim_path = "/" bool Checks whether a prim exists. Get Prim Typeusd:get_prim_type stageprim_path = "/" string Gets the schema type of a prim. Get Childrenusd:get_children stageprim_path = "/" list Lists the paths of the children of a prim. Get Parentusd:get_parent stageprim_path = "/" string Gets the path of the parent of a prim. Find Primsusd:find_prims stagename_patterntype_name list Finds the prims whose name matches a regular expression. Rename Primusd:rename_prim stageprim_path = "/"new_name stage Renames a prim in the layer the stage edits. Move Primusd:move_prim stageprim_path = "/"new_parent_path = "/" stage Moves a prim under another parent in the layer the stage edits. Copy Primusd:copy_prim stageprim_path = "/"new_path stage Copies a prim and what is below it in the layer the stage edits. Set Activeusd:set_active stageprim_path = "/"active = True stage Activates or deactivates a prim. Inactive prims are left out of traversals. Set Kindusd:set_kind stageprim_path = "/"kind = "component" stage Sets the kind of a prim, like component or assembly. Set Prim Metadatausd:set_prim_metadata stageprim_path = "/"keyvalue stage Sets a metadata field of a prim, like documentation or customData. Get Prim Metadatausd:get_prim_metadata stageprim_path = "/"key any Gets a metadata field of a prim.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Add Prim creates the prims above the one you ask for without a type. Add a parent first, as an Xform, if you want to transform it.
  • List Prims and Find Prims skip inactive prims (see Set Active) and abstract ones, such as classes.
  • Find Prims takes a regular expression and searches it in the name of the prims, not in their whole path: cube_\d+ finds /a/cube_01 and /b/cube_02.
  • Get Parent gives / for a prim at the top.
  • Rename, Move and Copy Prim edit the layer the stage edits, the root layer of a stage you opened. They fail with the reason from USD if the new name exists or the prim only exists through a reference or payload.
  • Set Kind takes the kinds of USD: component, group, assembly, subcomponent.
  • Set Prim Metadata and Get Prim Metadata work on fields like documentation, comment and customData (a dictionary). A value of the wrong type for the key fails. Some keys have schema defaults, customData of a transformable prim includes userDocBrief.

docs.title: Stage setting nodes
docs.text:
Tags: stage, settings, time, metadata

Metadata and settings of the stage as a whole: time, axis, units and the default prim.

Node Inputs Output What it does Set Stage Metadatausd:set_stage_metadata stagekeyvalue stage Sets a metadata field of the stage, like comment or documentation. Get Stage Metadatausd:get_stage_metadata stagekey any Gets a metadata field of the stage. Set Time Rangeusd:set_time_range stagestart = 0.0end = 100.0 stage Sets the first and last time code of the stage. Get Time Rangeusd:get_time_range stage list Gets the first and last time code of the stage. Set FPSusd:set_fps stagefps = 24.0 stage Sets the frames per second of the stage. Set Up Axisusd:set_up_axis stageaxis = "Y" stage Sets the up axis of the stage. Set Meters Per Unitusd:set_meters_per_unit stagemeters = 1.0 stage Sets the size of a unit of the stage in meters, 0.01 for centimeters. Set Default Primusd:set_default_prim stageprim_path = "/" stage Sets the prim used when the file is referenced without a target. Get Stage Infousd:get_stage_info stage dict Describes a stage: root layer, default prim, axis, units, time and prim count.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Set Up Axis takes Y or Z.
  • Set Meters Per Unit is the size of one unit in meters: 1 for meters, 0.01 for centimeters.
  • Set FPS sets the frames per second and the time codes per second together.
  • Set Time Range and Get Time Range work on the first and last time code. The end can't be before the start.
  • Set Default Prim names the prim that is used when the file is referenced without a target prim, see Add Reference.
  • Get Stage Info gives a dictionary with root_layer, default_prim (empty if there is none), up_axis, meters_per_unit, fps, start, end and prim_count.
  • Set Stage Metadata works on fields like comment and documentation.

docs.title: Stage nodes
docs.text:
Tags: stage

Open a file or create a stage, save it, and close it. The other nodes work on the stage handle these give, see Using the nodes.

Node Inputs Output What it does Open Stageusd:open_stage path stage Opens a USD file in the client. Create Stageusd:create_stage path stage Creates a stage in the client, in memory if no file is given. Save Stageusd:save_stage stagepath stage Saves a stage to its file, or exports it to the given one. Close Stageusd:close_stage stage none Closes a stage in the client without saving it.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Create Stage without a path makes a stage in memory. Give a path to have a file to Save Stage to, or give the path when saving.
  • Save Stage with an empty path saves the file the stage was opened from or created with. With a path it exports the stage there and the original file is left alone.
  • Open Stage fails with the reason from USD when the file can't be opened.
  • A stage stays open in the client until Close Stage, see Starting a client.
